lessons.summary: Communicate about identity and relationships with controlled tense, agreement and supporting detail.
objectives: Explain relationships with reasons and examples.
Move between present and past experience.
keyIdeas: Adjectives usually agree with the noun they describe.
Connectors turn separate facts into sustained communication.
A clear message matters more than forcing unfamiliar complexity.

definitions.meaning: Agreement in gender and number between related words.
A word or phrase that links ideas, such as aunque, por eso or sin embargo.
A viewpoint supported by a reason or example.

method: Identify audience, purpose and required tense.
Plan one main idea per sentence group.
Add reasons with porque, ya que or dado que.
Check verb endings and adjective agreement.

workedExample.prompt: Describe a friendship and explain why it matters.
steps: Opening: Mi amistad con Ana es importante para mí.
Detail: Nos conocemos desde hace cinco años y compartimos el interés por la música.
Reason: Aunque no siempre estamos de acuerdo, me escucha cuando tengo un problema.
workedExample.conclusion: The response communicates relationship, time, shared experience and a justified personal view.

misconceptions.mistake: Translating English word order directly.
misconceptions.correction: Build the Spanish phrase around its own agreement and placement patterns.

misconceptions.mistake: Using porque and por qué interchangeably.
misconceptions.correction: Porque gives a reason; por qué introduces or embeds a question.

practice.prompt: Escribe cuatro frases sobre tu personalidad y tus intereses. Puedes inventar los detalles.
solution: Possible fictional response: Soy una persona tranquila, pero a veces hablo mucho. Me interesa la música porque me ayuda a relajarme. En mi tiempo libre dibujo. Mis amigos dicen que soy amable.
Other coherent descriptions with four sentences and a reason are valid.

practice.prompt: Explica cómo ha cambiado una relación importante en tu vida. Puedes inventar una situación.
hints: Use a past reference and a present comparison.
solution: Possible fictional response: Antes hablaba poco con mi prima. El año pasado hicimos un proyecto juntas. Ahora hablamos más porque tenemos intereses comunes.
Juntas describes two female participants in this model; juntos is appropriate for a different relevant group. Other coherent accounts are valid.

practice.prompt: ¿Las redes sociales fortalecen o debilitan las amistades?
hints: Give both a benefit and a limitation.
solution: Possible response: Creo que las redes sociales pueden fortalecer las amistades porque permiten mantener el contacto. Por ejemplo, puedo escribir a un amigo que vive lejos. Sin embargo, los mensajes no siempre sustituyen una conversación en persona. Su efecto depende de cómo las usemos.
Alternative supported positions are valid; this is a model opinion, not a research finding.

practice.prompt: Translate: “My friends are generous because they share their ideas.”
hints: Use porque to introduce the reason.
solution: Mis amigos son generosos.
Porque comparten sus ideas supplies the reason.
Combined: Mis amigos son generosos porque comparten sus ideas.
successCriteria: Porque comparten sus ideas supplies the reason.
Combined: Mis amigos son generosos porque comparten sus ideas.

practice.prompt: Correct and explain: “Soy amigo de Pablo desde hace 2024.”
hints: A year is a starting point.
solution: 2024 identifies a starting year rather than a duration.
Use desde without hace.
Correct: Soy amigo de Pablo desde 2024.
successCriteria: 2024 identifies a starting year rather than a duration.
Correct: Soy amigo de Pablo desde 2024.

checklist: I check agreement and high-frequency verbs.

notes.title: Identity and relationships in context
paragraphs: Describing relationships requires more than a list of adjectives. Match adjectives to the person described, explain a shared activity, and support an opinion with porque or ya que. Me llevo bien con means that you get on well with someone; it describes the relationship rather than physical movement. A contrast introduced by aunque can add nuance without becoming a negative judgement. Keep references clear when several people are mentioned. In present-tense descriptions, desde hace introduces a duration that continues now, while desde identifies a starting point.

workedExamples.prompt: Original task: describe an ongoing friendship of two years, a shared activity and one difference.
steps: State the duration: Soy amiga de Lucía desde hace dos años.
Add common ground and contrast: Jugamos al tenis juntas, aunque yo prefiero los partidos cortos.
workedExamples.conclusion: “Me llevo bien con Lucía porque respeta mis opiniones” supplies a reason for the positive relationship.

flashcards.front: How do you say “I get on well with my brother”?
flashcards.back: Me llevo bien con mi hermano.

flashcards.front: What follows desde hace?
flashcards.back: A duration, such as dos años, for a situation continuing now.

flashcards.front: What does aunque introduce?
flashcards.back: A contrast or concession: aunque somos diferentes, nos llevamos bien.

flashcards.front: How does porque improve a description?
flashcards.back: It connects an opinion to a reason.

diagrams.title: Identity and relationships: relationships to explain
diagrams.description: Description → Evidence → Relationship. The reason explains the relationship judgement.

nodes.label: Relationship
nodes.detail: Por eso me llevo bien con ella.

edges.label: An action supports the adjective.
The reason explains the relationship judgement.

lessons.summary: Choose past forms by meaning: completed events, background description, repeated action and relevance to now.
objectives: Use time markers as clues rather than automatic rules.
keyIdeas: The preterite presents an event as bounded or completed.
The imperfect presents background, ongoing or habitual past action.
A writer can change tense to change viewpoint.

definitions.meaning: A past tense commonly presenting completed, bounded events.
A past tense commonly presenting background, ongoing or habitual situations.
A phrase that locates or sequences an event in time.

method: Decide whether the verb advances events or supplies background.
Choose the tense for that meaning.
Conjugate for the correct subject.
Use connectors to make sequence and contrast explicit.

workedExample.prompt: Complete to describe studying in progress interrupted by a completed call: Mientras yo ___ (estudiar), mi amigo me ___ (llamar).
steps: Studying is the ongoing background, so use estudiaba.
The call is the bounded interrupting event, so use llamó.
Full sentence: Mientras yo estudiaba, mi amigo me llamó.
workedExample.conclusion: The tense contrast shows an action in progress interrupted by a completed event.

misconceptions.mistake: Using one past tense for an entire narrative.
misconceptions.correction: Choose tense separately for each verb’s role in the scene.

misconceptions.mistake: Treating ayer as proof that every verb must be preterite.
misconceptions.correction: Time markers help, but aspect and intended viewpoint decide the tense.

practice.prompt: Complete to describe a repeated childhood habit: Cuando éramos niños, cada verano nosotros ___ (visitar) a nuestros abuelos.
solution: Visitábamos is appropriate for the repeated childhood habit specified in the prompt.

practice.prompt: Explain the tense contrast in “Hacía sol cuando empezó la tormenta.”
solution: Hacía uses imperfect for background weather.
Empezó uses preterite for the bounded event that advances the narrative.

practice.prompt: Write four connected Spanish sentences about an interrupted journey, using both preterite and imperfect.
solution: Example: Viajábamos en tren y todos dormían. De repente, el tren se paró. El conductor anunció un problema. Esperamos una hora antes de continuar.

practice.prompt: Translate “Yesterday I bought bread while my sister was studying.”
hints: Use mientras for the ongoing background.
solution: Ayer compré pan uses the preterite for the purchase.
Mientras mi hermana estudiaba uses the imperfect for the background.
Combined: Ayer compré pan mientras mi hermana estudiaba.
successCriteria: Ayer compré pan uses the preterite for the purchase.
Mientras mi hermana estudiaba uses the imperfect for the background.
Combined: Ayer compré pan mientras mi hermana estudiaba.

practice.prompt: Explain the difference between “Vivía allí” and “Viví allí cinco años”.
hints: Which version states a bounded duration?
Do not equate tense with short versus long.
solution: Vivía allí presents living there as background or an ongoing past situation.
Viví allí cinco años presents a completed five-year period.
The difference is viewpoint and boundedness, not whether five years is a short time.
successCriteria: Vivía allí presents living there as background or an ongoing past situation.
Viví allí cinco años presents a completed five-year period.
The difference is viewpoint and boundedness, not whether five years is a short time.

checklist: I connect sentences into a sequence.

notes.title: Past tenses in context
paragraphs: The preterite presents a past event as completed or bounded; the imperfect presents background, habitual action or an action in progress without focusing on its endpoint. Time expressions help but do not mechanically determine the tense. A speaker can describe a bounded period with the preterite even if an activity lasted a long time. In a narrative, the imperfect often sets the scene and the preterite advances events. Learn the actual verb forms as well as the distinction: an accurate choice of tense still needs the correct person and ending.

workedExamples.prompt: Original task: translate “When we arrived, it was raining and the guide was waiting for us.”
steps: Use a completed arrival: Cuando llegamos.
Use background conditions: llovía y el guía nos esperaba.
workedExamples.conclusion: Cuando llegamos, llovía y el guía nos esperaba. The arrival is bounded; rain and waiting form the scene.

flashcards.front: What does the preterite emphasise?
flashcards.back: A past event viewed as completed or bounded.

flashcards.front: What does the imperfect often supply?
flashcards.back: Background, habitual action or an ongoing past situation.

flashcards.front: Translate “I used to read every night”.
flashcards.back: Leía todas las noches.

flashcards.front: Is every long past action imperfect?
flashcards.back: No; a long action can be presented as a bounded completed event.

diagrams.title: Past tenses: relationships to explain
diagrams.description: Background → Event → Continuing scene. The arrival is placed within an existing situation.

edges.label: The weather forms the setting for arrival.
The arrival is placed within an existing situation.

lessons.summary: Build present-tense sentences with correct subjects, common endings and agreement in familiar contexts.
objectives: Distinguish a routine from an action happening now.
explanation: This lesson assumes that you can recognise basic subject pronouns and familiar nouns. The present indicative can describe habits and current situations: Estudio español means I study Spanish, and context can also support I am studying Spanish. Regular endings depend on the infinitive group and subject. For regular verbs, remove -ar, -er or -ir and add endings for the subject. In the order yo, tú, él/ella/usted, nosotros/nosotras, vosotros/vosotras, ellos/ellas/ustedes, the -ar endings are -o, -as, -a, -amos, -áis, -an; -er endings are -o, -es, -e, -emos, -éis, -en; -ir endings are -o, -es, -e, -imos, -ís, -en. Thus tú comes means you eat, and mis amigas viven means my female friends live. Nosotros forms are hablamos, comemos and vivimos. Ustedes takes the third-person plural form and is the usual plural you in Latin America; vosotros is common for informal plural you in Spain. Subject pronouns are often omitted when the verb and context identify the speaker.

Do not copy an English auxiliary into every present sentence. Estudio todos los días is a natural statement of routine. Estoy estudiando ahora emphasises an activity in progress, but this lesson focuses on the simple present. Check irregular forms separately, and make adjectives agree with the nouns they describe. The examples are original teaching sentences, not descriptions of actual learners; valid regional pronouns and forms should be judged within the variety being practised.
keyIdeas: Choose the subject before the ending.
Spanish often omits an understood subject pronoun.
Meaning and context guide tense choice.

definitions.meaning: The dictionary form, such as hablar, comer or vivir.
A verb form used for present situations, habits and other context-dependent meanings.
Agreement between the verb and its subject in person and number.

method: Identify who performs the action.
Find the infinitive and its group.
Choose the present ending or check an irregular form.
Read the complete sentence for meaning and agreement.

workedExample.prompt: Original exercise: complete “Nosotras ___ (vivir) cerca de la escuela” in the present indicative.
steps: The subject nosotras requires first-person plural.
Vivir is an -ir verb; the form is vivimos.
Nosotras vivimos cerca de la escuela means We live near the school.
workedExample.conclusion: Vivimos matches the subject. Nosotras may be omitted when the context is clear.

misconceptions.mistake: Using the infinitive as the main verb after a subject.
misconceptions.correction: Conjugate it: yo hablo, not yo hablar.

misconceptions.mistake: Adding estoy to a routine without changing the following verb.
misconceptions.correction: Use Estudio cada día, or the appropriate estar + gerund construction for an ongoing action.

practice.prompt: Complete in the present: “Tú ___ (comer) en casa.”
hints: Use the tú ending for an -er verb.
solution: Tú comes en casa.
You eat at home.

practice.prompt: Correct agreement: “Mis amigas vive en una casa pequeño.”
hints: Check the plural subject and the feminine singular noun casa.
solution: Mis amigas viven en una casa pequeña.
Viven agrees with mis amigas; pequeña agrees with casa.

practice.prompt: Write three Spanish sentences about a fictional daily routine using three different present verbs.
hints: Use familiar activities and time expressions.
solution: Possible response: Desayuno a las siete. Voy a la escuela en autobús. Por la tarde, leo en casa.
Meaning: I have breakfast at seven, go to school by bus and read at home in the afternoon. Other coherent routines are valid.

practice.prompt: Translate “My sister and I eat at home on Fridays.”
hints: Two people including the speaker use nosotros/nosotras.
solution: Mi hermana y yo is a plural first-person subject.
The correct form is comemos.
Mi hermana y yo comemos en casa los viernes.
successCriteria: Mi hermana y yo is a plural first-person subject.
Mi hermana y yo comemos en casa los viernes.

practice.prompt: Correct “Ellos vive cerca, pero no hablan mucho.” Explain the correction.
solution: Ellos requires a third-person plural verb.
Vive must become viven.
Correct: Ellos viven cerca, pero no hablan mucho.
successCriteria: Ellos requires a third-person plural verb.
Correct: Ellos viven cerca, pero no hablan mucho.

notes.title: Present tense in context
paragraphs: The present indicative describes current situations, habitual actions and general statements. Spanish verb endings usually identify the subject, so subject pronouns can be omitted when the reference is clear. Regular -ar, -er and -ir verbs follow different ending patterns, but many common verbs are irregular. Negation normally places no before the conjugated verb. Frequency phrases such as a menudo or los lunes clarify habitual meaning. Check that the verb agrees with the subject rather than the nearest noun, especially when a sentence includes a description of someone else.

workedExamples.prompt: Original task: say that we write in Spanish on Mondays but do not read aloud every day.
steps: Conjugate escribir for nosotros: escribimos; los lunes marks a weekly habit.
Conjugate leer for nosotros and place no before it: no leemos en voz alta todos los días.
workedExamples.conclusion: Los lunes escribimos en español, pero no leemos en voz alta todos los días.

flashcards.front: What is the nosotros form of escribir?
flashcards.back: Escribimos.

flashcards.front: Where does no normally go?
flashcards.back: Immediately before the conjugated verb or its preceding object pronouns.

flashcards.front: What does los martes express?
flashcards.back: A recurring habit on Tuesdays.

flashcards.front: Must a Spanish subject pronoun always be stated?
flashcards.back: No; the ending and context often identify the subject.

diagrams.title: Present tense: relationships to explain
diagrams.description: Subject → Verb agreement → Frequency. A frequency phrase specifies the habitual pattern.

edges.label: The subject selects the verb ending.
A frequency phrase specifies the habitual pattern.

lessons.summary: Use common irregular verbs and distinguish identity, location, existence, possession and liking.
objectives: Make gustar agree with the thing liked.
explanation: Common verbs need repeated practice in meaningful sentences. Soy estudiante identifies the speaker as a student; estoy en la biblioteca locates the speaker. The shortcut permanent versus temporary is unreliable: location normally uses estar even for a building. Hay introduces existence, as in Hay dos salas. Las salas están arriba then locates those identified rooms. Tener expresses possession and age: Tengo quince años means I am fifteen years old.

With gustar in its ordinary liking construction, the liked thing is the grammatical subject. Me gusta el libro uses singular gusta, while Me gustan los libros uses plural gustan. The pronoun me identifies the person who likes it. Learn useful irregular forms such as tengo, hago, voy, quiero and puedo in context. A following infinitive normally stays unconjugated: Puedo leer means I can read. These selected patterns are a foundation, not a full account of every use of ser or estar.
keyIdeas: Match verb choice to meaning.
Hay introduces existence and does not become plural here.
Gustar agrees with the liked thing.

definitions.meaning: The impersonal present form of haber used to state that something exists.
A verb used here to locate someone or something already identified.
In these examples, to be pleasing to someone, expressed naturally in English as liking.

method: Decide whether the message concerns existence, location or another meaning.
Choose the verb and subject.
Check irregular forms and gustar agreement.
Translate the whole meaning rather than each word separately.

workedExample.prompt: Original exercise: translate “There are two books. The books are on the table. I like the books.”
steps: Existence: Hay dos libros.
Location: Los libros están en la mesa.
Liking: Me gustan los libros.
workedExample.conclusion: Hay remains unchanged for plural existence; están and gustan agree with los libros.

misconceptions.mistake: Writing me gusta los libros.
misconceptions.correction: Use gustan for the plural subject los libros.

misconceptions.mistake: Explaining ser and estar only as permanent and temporary.
misconceptions.correction: Use the relevant construction and meaning; location is normally expressed with estar.

practice.prompt: Complete: “Yo ___ (tener) quince años y ___ (ir) a la escuela.”
solution: Yo tengo quince años y voy a la escuela.
I am fifteen years old and I go to school.

practice.prompt: Correct: “Hay tres libros y me gusta los libros.”
hints: Hay is already correct; check the liked thing.
solution: Hay tres libros y me gustan los libros.
A more natural version in context is Hay tres libros y me gustan.

practice.prompt: Translate “I can read, but I want to write” into Spanish.
hints: Keep the second verb in each pair as an infinitive.
solution: Puedo leer, pero quiero escribir.
Yo puedo leer, pero quiero escribir is also valid when the subject needs emphasis.

practice.prompt: Translate “I like the book, but I prefer the films.”
solution: Me gusta el libro uses singular gusta.
Pero introduces the contrast.
Me gusta el libro, pero prefiero las películas.
successCriteria: Me gusta el libro uses singular gusta.
Me gusta el libro, pero prefiero las películas.

practice.prompt: Correct “Hay dos chicas y las chicas es cansadas.”
hints: Cansadas describes the girls’ state here; use estar with plural agreement.
solution: Hay dos chicas correctly expresses existence.
Las chicas requires están and a plural adjective.
Correct: Hay dos chicas y las chicas están cansadas.
successCriteria: Hay dos chicas correctly expresses existence.
Las chicas requires están and a plural adjective.
Correct: Hay dos chicas y las chicas están cansadas.

notes.title: High-frequency verbs in context
paragraphs: High-frequency verbs carry different grammatical patterns. Ser often identifies or characterises, while estar often locates people or objects and expresses states; the distinction is not simply permanent versus temporary. Hay presents existence without agreeing with the noun that follows. Tener expresses possession and several conditions, including age. With gustar, the liked thing controls singular gusta or plural gustan, while me, te or le identifies the experiencer. Practise these verbs in complete sentences so the meaning and agreement stay connected.

workedExamples.prompt: Original task: translate “There is a café. It is near the school. I like its windows.”
steps: Present existence with hay: Hay una cafetería. Locate it with está: Está cerca de la escuela.
The plural ventanas controls gustan: Me gustan sus ventanas.
workedExamples.conclusion: Hay una cafetería. Está cerca de la escuela. Me gustan sus ventanas.

flashcards.front: How do you express existence?
flashcards.back: Hay: Hay un libro / Hay dos libros.

flashcards.front: What controls gusta or gustan?
flashcards.back: The singular or plural thing that is liked.

flashcards.front: Translate “I am fifteen years old”.
flashcards.back: Tengo quince años.

flashcards.front: Is ser versus estar only permanent versus temporary?
flashcards.back: No; identity, location, state and other uses determine the choice.

diagrams.title: High-frequency verbs: relationships to explain
diagrams.description: Existence → Location → Preference. A preference adds the speaker’s response to a feature.

edges.label: After introducing a place, locate it.
A preference adds the speaker’s response to a feature.

lessons.summary: Narrate an original experience using past events, background detail and a clear personal response.
objectives: Explain an opinion with a reason.
explanation: A short account needs a setting, an event and a response. Use the preterite for events presented as bounded: Llegamos tarde means We arrived late. Use the imperfect for background or an ongoing situation: Llovía means It was raining. This is a choice of viewpoint, not a rule that every short action takes one tense and every long action another. Time markers help readers follow the sequence but do not choose the tense automatically.

Keep details consistent across sentences and justify the response with because or another appropriate connector. You may invent the experience for practice. There is no need to disclose a personal event. Present perfect and simple past usage differs across Spanish-speaking regions, so a valid local choice should not be rejected merely for differing from one model. These tasks specify a completed past setting and practise preterite and imperfect contrasts within that frame.
keyIdeas: Set the scene before sequencing events.
Tense expresses viewpoint.
An opinion needs supporting detail.

definitions.meaning: An event or situation someone has lived through or, here, a fictional account for practice.
The preterite, used here to present bounded past events.
A past form used here for background or an ongoing past situation.

method: Identify the completed past setting.
Separate background from events.
Link events in a clear sequence.
Add a reasoned reaction and check forms.

workedExample.prompt: Original fictional account: express “It was raining. We visited a museum. I liked the visit because I learned something new.”
steps: Background: Llovía.
Event: Visitamos un museo.
Reaction: Me gustó la visita porque aprendí algo nuevo.
workedExample.conclusion: The account combines background, a completed visit and a reasoned reaction.

misconceptions.mistake: Using the imperfect only because an action lasted a long time.
misconceptions.correction: Duration alone does not determine aspect.

misconceptions.mistake: Giving an opinion without a reason.
misconceptions.correction: Add a relevant detail with porque.

practice.prompt: Translate “Yesterday I visited a museum with my sister” into Spanish.
hints: Use the first-person preterite of visitar.
solution: Ayer visité un museo con mi hermana.
Visité needs its written accent.

practice.prompt: Explain in English the contrast in this original sentence: “Hacía frío, pero jugamos en el parque.”
hints: Distinguish background from the bounded activity.
solution: Hacía frío supplies background: it was cold.
Jugamos presents playing in the park as a completed past event in this context.
Pero introduces contrast: despite the cold, we played.

practice.prompt: Write three connected Spanish sentences about a fictional past outing, using one imperfect form, one preterite event and a reasoned opinion.
hints: Describe conditions, report an event, then give a reason.
solution: Possible response: Hacía sol. Fuimos al parque y jugamos al fútbol. Me gustó la tarde porque pasé tiempo con mis amigos.
Other coherent outings meeting the tense and reasoning requirements are valid.

practice.prompt: Original task: say “First we visited the market. Afterwards we ate in the park.”
solution: Primero visitamos el mercado.
Después comimos en el parque.
The connectors establish the order of two completed activities.
successCriteria: The connectors establish the order of two completed activities.

practice.prompt: Expand “El viaje fue bueno” with a specific reason about meeting new people.
solution: El viaje fue bueno states an evaluation.
Porque conocí a gente nueva gives a specific reason.
Combined: El viaje fue bueno porque conocí a gente nueva.
successCriteria: El viaje fue bueno states an evaluation.
Porque conocí a gente nueva gives a specific reason.
Combined: El viaje fue bueno porque conocí a gente nueva.

checklist: I keep the time frame clear.

notes.title: Experiences in context
paragraphs: A clear account of an experience gives the reader a sequence, a setting and a response. Use a small number of accurate connectors such as primero, después and al final rather than beginning every sentence with y. The preterite can move events forward while the imperfect supplies background. Explain an opinion with a detail from the experience: fue interesante is more informative when followed by what you learned or noticed. Do not add a dramatic event merely to demonstrate a tense; coherence matters as much as grammatical variety.

workedExamples.prompt: Original fictional account: describe arriving late at a workshop, being welcomed and learning to draw a map.
steps: Introduce the event and response: Llegué tarde al taller, pero la profesora me recibió con amabilidad.
Add learning and evaluation: Aprendí a dibujar un mapa y me gustó comparar las rutas.
workedExamples.conclusion: The account gives a sequence and a reason for interest without relying on a list of disconnected tense forms.

flashcards.front: What does después mark?
flashcards.back: An event occurring later in the sequence.

flashcards.front: How can an opinion become specific?
flashcards.back: Give a reason linked to something experienced.

flashcards.front: What tense often supplies a narrative setting?
flashcards.back: The imperfect.

flashcards.front: What should a short experience account contain?
flashcards.back: A coherent sequence, relevant context and a justified response.

diagrams.title: Experiences: relationships to explain
diagrams.description: Arrival → Activity → Evaluation. The evaluation refers to a concrete part of the experience.

edges.label: The arrival situates the activity.
The evaluation refers to a concrete part of the experience.

lessons.summary: Distinguish plans, future statements and polite conditional requests without confusing their verb patterns.
objectives: Use selected future and conditional forms.
Build a real future condition with present after si.
explanation: Ir a plus infinitive is a common way to express an intention or prospective action: Voy a estudiar means I am going to study. The a is part of this construction. The simple future adds endings to an infinitive or an irregular future stem: estudiaré, tendré. A future form does not guarantee that an event will happen; context determines whether it is a prediction, promise or other future statement.

The conditional uses endings such as -ía and can make a request more polite: ¿Podrías repetirlo? means Could you repeat it? This lesson introduces these familiar uses without requiring a full hypothetical subjunctive system. In the real condition Si tengo tiempo, estudiaré, use present tengo after si, not future tendré. Keep the unaccented conjunction si distinct from sí meaning yes. Future and conditional forms also have other uses beyond this introductory scope.
keyIdeas: Keep a in ir a + infinitive.
Future and conditional convey different meanings.
Real future conditions use present after si in this pattern.

definitions.meaning: A form used here for a future statement, such as estudiaré.
A form used here for a polite request or a would meaning, such as podría.
A construction used here for an intended or prospective action.

method: Decide whether the message is a plan, statement or request.
Choose the construction.
Check the subject, stem, ending and required preposition.
Read any si clause and preserve the intended meaning.

workedExample.prompt: Original exercise: express “Tomorrow I am going to study. Could you help me?” using informal tú.
steps: Plan: Mañana voy a estudiar.
Polite request: ¿Podrías ayudarme?
Voy a is followed by the infinitive; podrías has a written accent and tú agreement.
workedExample.conclusion: Mañana voy a estudiar. ¿Podrías ayudarme? The request does not assert that help will occur.

misconceptions.mistake: Omitting a in voy a estudiar.
misconceptions.correction: Retain the preposition in this construction.

misconceptions.mistake: Using si tendré tiempo for this real future condition.
misconceptions.correction: Use Si tengo tiempo, estudiaré.

practice.prompt: Complete the plan: “Nosotros vamos ___ visitar el museo.”
solution: Nosotros vamos a visitar el museo.
We are going to visit the museum.

practice.prompt: Translate “I will have time tomorrow” using tener in the simple future tense.
solution: Tendré tiempo mañana.
Yo tendré tiempo mañana is also valid with an explicit subject.

practice.prompt: Write a Spanish sentence meaning “If I have time, I will read”, using the simple future tense for leer, then a polite tú request meaning “Could you repeat it?”
hints: Use present after si and conditional poder for the request.
solution: Si tengo tiempo, leeré.
¿Podrías repetirlo?
Repetir eso may replace repetirlo if the intended reference is clear.

practice.prompt: Correct “Voy a escribo una carta mañana.”
hints: The future meaning is already carried by voy a.
solution: Escribo is a conjugated present form.
Replace it with escribir.
Correct: Voy a escribir una carta mañana.
successCriteria: Escribo is a conjugated present form.
Correct: Voy a escribir una carta mañana.

practice.prompt: Translate “I would visit the museum, but I do not have time.”
hints: Keep the current obstacle in the present.
solution: Visitaría el museo expresses a hypothetical action.
Pero no tengo tiempo gives the present obstacle.
Combined: Visitaría el museo, pero no tengo tiempo.
successCriteria: Visitaría el museo expresses a hypothetical action.
Pero no tengo tiempo gives the present obstacle.
Combined: Visitaría el museo, pero no tengo tiempo.

notes.title: Future and conditional in context
paragraphs: Ir a plus an infinitive expresses a planned or anticipated action, while the simple future can state future events and other meanings depending on context. Keep the infinitive after a: voy a estudiar, not voy a estudio. The conditional can describe a hypothetical outcome or soften a request. Distinguish intention from certainty; saying that someone plans to act does not prove the action will occur. In polite classroom requests, podrías with tú and podría with usted make the relationship explicit through the verb form.

workedExamples.prompt: Original task: state a plan to practise tomorrow and politely ask a friend to read your draft.
steps: Use a planned action: Mañana voy a practicar.
Use an informal conditional request: ¿Podrías leer mi borrador?
workedExamples.conclusion: Mañana voy a practicar. ¿Podrías leer mi borrador? The plan and request serve different communicative functions.

flashcards.front: What follows ir a in a future plan?
flashcards.back: An infinitive, such as estudiar.

flashcards.front: Translate “We are going to write”.
flashcards.back: Vamos a escribir.

flashcards.front: How can the conditional soften a request?
flashcards.back: ¿Podrías ayudarme? asks whether a friend could help.

flashcards.front: What distinguishes podría and podrías in a request?
flashcards.back: Podría can address usted; podrías addresses tú.

diagrams.description: Plan → Needed support → Polite request. The conditional frames the request politely.

nodes.detail: Queremos una opinión sobre el texto.

lessons.summary: Describe the purpose of an invention and discuss a benefit and limitation in clear, qualified Spanish.
objectives: Explain purpose with para plus infinitive.
Balance a benefit with a limitation.
explanation: This theme provides language for discussing inventions, media and communication. Explain what a tool does before evaluating it. Para plus infinitive expresses purpose when appropriate: Uso una aplicación para organizar mis tareas means I use an app to organise my tasks. The infinitive after para does not change to match the speaker. A description can then add a personal benefit with porque and a limitation with pero or sin embargo.

Keep claims within the fictional scenario or clearly mark them as opinions. Puede ayudar means it can help, which is weaker than a guarantee. Avoid inventing a scientific result to make a language answer sound convincing. You can describe a simple tool without advanced technical vocabulary. In open tasks, different inventions and valid regional words are acceptable if the explanation is coherent and the grammar communicates the required functions.
keyIdeas: State function before evaluation.
Para + infinitive expresses purpose.
Qualified language avoids unsupported guarantees.

definitions.meaning: An invention or newly devised object or process.
A phrase expressing purpose, such as para escribir.
A benefit or favourable feature in a stated context.

method: Name the tool and its user.
Explain its purpose with a suitable construction.
Add a benefit and limitation.
Check infinitives, agreement and strength of claims.

workedExample.prompt: Original fictional scenario: explain an app used to organise homework, with one limitation.
steps: Purpose: Uso una aplicación para organizar mis tareas.
Benefit: Me ayuda a recordar las fechas.
Limit: Sin embargo, necesito una conexión a internet.
workedExample.conclusion: The response describes a use and a specific constraint rather than claiming the app always improves results.

misconceptions.mistake: Conjugating after para in para organizo.
misconceptions.correction: Use para organizar for this purpose construction.

misconceptions.mistake: Giving an absolute claim without support.
misconceptions.correction: Use a scoped statement such as puede ayudar or en este caso.

practice.prompt: Complete: “Uso el ordenador para ___ (escribir).”
solution: Uso el ordenador para escribir.
I use the computer to write. Computadora is a valid regional alternative to ordenador.

practice.prompt: Translate “This tool is useful, but it is expensive.” The tool is una herramienta.
hints: Make both adjectives agree with herramienta.
solution: Esta herramienta es útil, pero es cara.
Útil does not change for feminine gender; cara does.

practice.prompt: Describe a fictional invention in three Spanish sentences: its purpose, a possible benefit and a limitation.
hints: Use para, puede and pero if helpful.
solution: Possible response: Este robot sirve para ordenar libros. Puede ahorrar tiempo. Pero necesita electricidad.
Other coherent inventions are valid; no real performance claim is required.

practice.prompt: Translate “The website helps me learn words, but it does not replace conversation.”
hints: Use me ayuda a plus infinitive.
Use pero to limit the claim.
solution: La página web me ayuda a aprender palabras.
Pero no sustituye la conversación supplies the limit.
Combined: La página web me ayuda a aprender palabras, pero no sustituye la conversación.
successCriteria: La página web me ayuda a aprender palabras.
Pero no sustituye la conversación supplies the limit.
Combined: La página web me ayuda a aprender palabras, pero no sustituye la conversación.

practice.prompt: Original scenario: a fictional translation tool gives two possible meanings. Write a Spanish response explaining why context is needed.
hints: Explain choosing rather than accepting blindly.
solution: La herramienta ofrece dos significados.
Necesito leer el contexto.
Así puedo elegir la opción que corresponde a la frase.
successCriteria: Así puedo elegir la opción que corresponde a la frase.

notes.title: Human ingenuity in context
paragraphs: When discussing technology, explain a function before evaluating its value. Sirve para plus an infinitive identifies what something is used for, while permite can introduce what it enables a user to do. A balanced response gives a concrete benefit and a limitation rather than claiming that all technology is good or bad. Attribute statements about a fictional device to the supplied scenario. Familiar vocabulary can communicate a careful judgement: útil, rápido and cómodo need a reason, and sin embargo can introduce a relevant qualification.

workedExamples.prompt: Original fictional task: explain a reminder app that stores tasks on one device but does not synchronise them.
steps: State its function: La aplicación sirve para organizar las tareas.
Balance benefit and limit: Es útil para recordar las fechas; sin embargo, no sincroniza los datos entre dispositivos.
workedExamples.conclusion: The evaluation links usefulness and limitation to the app’s stated functions, not to unsupported claims about all apps.

flashcards.front: What follows sirve para?
flashcards.back: An infinitive describing purpose.

flashcards.front: Translate “It allows us to share ideas”.
flashcards.back: Nos permite compartir ideas.

flashcards.front: What does sin embargo introduce?
flashcards.back: A contrast or qualification: however.

flashcards.front: How can a technology opinion be justified?
flashcards.back: Connect it to a particular function and a stated limitation.

diagrams.description: Function → Benefit → Limit. The storage limit qualifies how convenient the app is.

nodes.detail: Los datos quedan en un dispositivo.

The storage limit qualifies how convenient the app is.

lessons.summary: Describe community services, locations and practical rules with clear language for existence and obligation.
objectives: Express a general requirement with hay que.
explanation: Community topics include schools, libraries, transport and shared activities. Introduce a service with hay, then locate it with estar: Hay una biblioteca; está al lado del parque. Al lado de means next to; de plus el contracts to del. These patterns communicate practical information without needing a long description. Keep locations consistent within an invented neighbourhood.

Hay que plus infinitive expresses a general requirement or necessity in the context: Hay que reservar means booking is required. Tengo que reservar identifies the speaker’s obligation instead. Rules in these exercises are fictional service rules, not claims about actual institutions or legal advice. When explaining a proposal, give a reason and consider access: a service may exist but be unavailable at a useful time. Alternative communities and regional vocabulary are acceptable in open writing tasks.
keyIdeas: Hay introduces existence.
Estar locates an identified place.
General and personal obligations use different patterns.

definitions.meaning: A service provided for users or a community.
Next to, expressing relative location.
An impersonal construction expressing a contextual requirement or necessity.

method: Identify the service and context.
State existence and location clearly.
Explain a relevant rule or proposal.
Check contractions, infinitives and access details.

workedExample.prompt: Original fictional notice: describe a library next to the park where booking is required.
steps: Existence: Hay una biblioteca.
Location: Está al lado del parque.
Rule: Hay que reservar antes de entrar.
workedExample.conclusion: The notice identifies the service, its location and the fictional booking rule.

misconceptions.mistake: Using plural forms of existential hay.
misconceptions.correction: Use Hay dos bibliotecas.

misconceptions.mistake: Omitting the infinitive after hay que.
misconceptions.correction: Use Hay que reservar, not Hay que reserva.

practice.prompt: Translate “There are two schools in my neighbourhood.”
solution: Hay dos escuelas en mi barrio.
Colegios can be appropriate where that word fits the intended type of school.

practice.prompt: Complete: “La biblioteca está al lado ___ parque.”
solution: La biblioteca está al lado del parque.
The library is next to the park.

practice.prompt: Write three Spanish sentences proposing a fictional community library: say what is missing, what you propose and why.
hints: Use no hay, propongo and porque.
solution: Possible response: En mi barrio no hay biblioteca. Propongo abrir una cerca de la escuela. Sería útil porque podríamos estudiar allí.
Other coherent proposals are valid; advanced conditional forms may be replaced with simpler accurate wording.

practice.prompt: Translate “You can study here, but you must book a table.” Use impersonal forms.
solution: Se puede estudiar aquí expresses permission or possibility.
Pero hay que reservar una mesa states the requirement.
Combined: Se puede estudiar aquí, pero hay que reservar una mesa.
successCriteria: Se puede estudiar aquí expresses permission or possibility.
Pero hay que reservar una mesa states the requirement.
Combined: Se puede estudiar aquí, pero hay que reservar una mesa.

practice.prompt: Original notice: “Entrada gratuita. Reserva obligatoria.” Explain in English and write a Spanish question about booking.
hints: Free entry does not remove the booking rule.
solution: Entry is free.
Booking is compulsory.
A suitable question is: ¿Cómo puedo reservar?
successCriteria: A suitable question is: ¿Cómo puedo reservar?

checklist: I use hay que with an infinitive.

notes.title: Social organisation in context
paragraphs: Describing community services requires accurate information about place, access and obligations. Se puede expresses what is possible or permitted, while hay que plus an infinitive expresses an impersonal requirement. Tener que identifies who must act. Keep opening times, prices and access rules tied to a supplied fictional notice rather than presenting them as current facts about a real institution. When requesting information, distinguish dónde, cuándo and cómo. A useful response includes the detail the other person needs to take the next step.

workedExamples.prompt: Original fictional notice: a club meets at the community centre on Tuesdays; participants must register beforehand.
steps: Locate the activity and time: El club se reúne en el centro comunitario los martes.
State the requirement: Hay que inscribirse antes de asistir.
workedExamples.conclusion: El club se reúne en el centro comunitario los martes. Hay que inscribirse antes de asistir.

flashcards.front: What does hay que express?
flashcards.back: An impersonal obligation or requirement.

flashcards.front: What follows tener que?
flashcards.back: An infinitive: tenemos que reservar.

flashcards.front: Translate “Where can I register?”
flashcards.back: ¿Dónde puedo inscribirme?

flashcards.front: Why distinguish a fictional notice from a real service?
flashcards.back: Its details belong to the exercise and are not verified current information.

diagrams.description: Service → Schedule → Access rule. The rule specifies what must happen before attendance.

nodes.detail: Un club en el centro comunitario.

edges.label: The schedule tells participants when the service operates.
The rule specifies what must happen before attendance.

lessons.summary: Express environmental routines and practical proposals without overstating the effects of a fictional action.
objectives: Describe a routine in the present.
Suggest an action with podemos plus infinitive.
Give a reason and a limitation.
explanation: This theme practises language about shared places and resources. Begin with a specific action: Reutilizo el papel means I reuse paper. Podemos plus infinitive makes a group suggestion: Podemos usar menos papel means We can use less paper. Menos does not change its ending to agree with papel. Use porque to explain a reason and pero to acknowledge a constraint.

A language response should not invent environmental statistics or guarantee that one action solves a global problem. Describe the fictional setting and use appropriately limited claims. Cuidar el parque means to look after the park; reducing waste and reusing materials are different actions. The tasks assess communication and grammar, not the environmental performance of a real intervention. Open responses may use another plausible action if they preserve the requested functions and avoid unsupported factual claims.
keyIdeas: Name a specific action.
Podemos takes an infinitive.
A proposal can include a limitation.

definitions.meaning: To use something again.
Waste materials in the context of these tasks.
We can followed by an action, used here to propose a group activity.

method: Identify the fictional issue and setting.
State an action in clear Spanish.
Explain a relevant reason or purpose.
Add a limitation and check grammar.

workedExample.prompt: Original fictional classroom proposal: suggest reusing paper and state a limitation.
steps: Suggestion: Podemos reutilizar el papel.
Purpose: Así usamos menos material nuevo.
Limit: Pero algunas hojas están demasiado dañadas.
workedExample.conclusion: The proposal is specific and qualified; it makes no quantified environmental claim.

misconceptions.mistake: Writing podemos usamos.
misconceptions.correction: Use the infinitive: podemos usar.

misconceptions.mistake: Claiming one small action solves every environmental problem.
misconceptions.correction: Keep the claim proportional to the scenario.

practice.prompt: Translate “We can use less paper.”
hints: Use poder followed by an infinitive.
solution: Podemos usar menos papel.

practice.prompt: Correct agreement: “Las botellas está vacíos.”
solution: Las botellas están vacías.
Están agrees with the plural subject; vacías agrees in gender and number.

practice.prompt: Write three Spanish sentences about a fictional school waste-reduction plan: an action, a reason and a limitation.
hints: Use a clear connector for each relationship.
solution: Possible response: Vamos a reutilizar las carpetas. Así compramos menos material. Sin embargo, necesitamos revisar su estado.
Other coherent plans are valid without invented impact statistics.

practice.prompt: Translate “We can share books because not everyone needs a new copy.”
hints: Use no todos for not everyone.
solution: Podemos compartir libros states the possibility.
Porque no todos necesitan un ejemplar nuevo gives the reason.
Combined: Podemos compartir libros porque no todos necesitan un ejemplar nuevo.
successCriteria: Podemos compartir libros states the possibility.
Porque no todos necesitan un ejemplar nuevo gives the reason.
Combined: Podemos compartir libros porque no todos necesitan un ejemplar nuevo.

practice.prompt: Improve “Reutilizar una bolsa elimina toda la contaminación” with a bounded Spanish claim.
hints: Replace eliminates all with can reduce.
solution: The original claim exaggerates the effect of one action.
A bounded version is: Reutilizar una bolsa puede reducir el uso de bolsas nuevas.
It describes a possible local reduction rather than the elimination of all pollution.
successCriteria: The original claim exaggerates the effect of one action.
A bounded version is: Reutilizar una bolsa puede reducir el uso de bolsas nuevas.
It describes a possible local reduction rather than the elimination of all pollution.

notes.title: Sharing the planet in context
paragraphs: Environmental discussion is clearer when a proposal names an action, a reason and a limitation. Podemos plus an infinitive suggests a shared possibility; deberíamos offers a recommendation. Avoid claiming that one small action solves an entire environmental problem. Use menos and más to compare quantities, and distinguish reducir from eliminar. In classroom proposals, concrete examples such as repairing an object or reusing a folder support meaningful language practice without requiring invented statistics. Connect a limitation with aunque or sin embargo so the response remains coherent.

workedExamples.prompt: Original fictional proposal: suggest repairing classroom folders before buying replacements, while recognising that some cannot be repaired.
steps: Propose an action: Podemos reparar las carpetas antes de comprar otras.
Qualify it: Así usamos menos materiales, aunque algunas carpetas no se pueden reparar.
workedExamples.conclusion: The proposal gives a plausible local benefit and a limit without claiming to eliminate all waste.

flashcards.front: Translate “We should reuse the boxes”.
flashcards.back: Deberíamos reutilizar las cajas.

flashcards.front: How does reducir differ from eliminar?
flashcards.back: Reducir means reduce; eliminar means remove or eliminate.

flashcards.front: What does menos materiales mean?
flashcards.back: Fewer materials or less material, depending on context.

flashcards.front: Why add a limitation?
flashcards.back: It makes a proposal more precise and avoids an exaggerated claim.

diagrams.title: Sharing the planet: relationships to explain
diagrams.description: Action → Local benefit → Limit. The condition limits when the proposed benefit applies.

edges.label: Repair can reduce the need for replacements.
The condition limits when the proposed benefit applies.

lessons.summary: Link Spanish ideas through cause, contrast, consequence and sequence while preserving the intended relationship.
explanation: Connectors tell the reader how ideas relate. Porque gives a reason: Estudio porque quiero aprender means I study because I want to learn. Por eso introduces a consequence: Quiero aprender; por eso estudio. Pero and sin embargo express contrast, while primero and después organise a sequence. Select the relationship before choosing a word; adding a sophisticated connector does not repair an illogical connection.

Por qué, written separately with an accent, asks why in direct or indirect questions: ¿Por qué estudias? and No sé por qué estudias. Porque, one word without an accent, gives a reason in these tasks. These are not the only porque-related forms, but they cover this lesson’s scope. Use commas or full stops to keep linked clauses readable. Open writing can use another accurate connector when it expresses the required relationship.
keyIdeas: Meaning determines the connector.
Porque and por qué differ in function.
Punctuation helps the reader follow a link.

definitions.meaning: A reason for an action or situation.
A result presented as following from another situation.
A relationship highlighting a difference or an unexpected combination.

method: Identify the relationship between ideas.
Choose a connector expressing it.
Preserve sentence order and punctuation.
Check spelling and accents.

workedExample.prompt: Original exercise: link “Quiero aprender español” and “practico cada día” as a consequence.
steps: The desire to learn is the stated reason.
Daily practice is presented as the consequence.
Quiero aprender español; por eso practico cada día.
workedExample.conclusion: Por eso marks the consequence. Practico cada día porque quiero aprender español expresses the same relationship in a different order.

misconceptions.mistake: Using por eso to introduce the reason itself.
misconceptions.correction: Check the direction of the relationship.

misconceptions.mistake: Writing porque in a direct why question.
misconceptions.correction: Use ¿Por qué...? with a space and accent.

practice.prompt: Complete the why question: “¿___ estudias español?”
solution: ¿Por qué estudias español?
Why do you study Spanish?

practice.prompt: Combine with contrast: “El libro es largo. Es interesante.”
solution: El libro es largo, pero es interesante.
El libro es largo. Sin embargo, es interesante. Both express the requested contrast.

practice.prompt: Write three Spanish sentences about a fictional study session, using primero, después and porque across the response.
hints: Organise two activities and explain one choice.
solution: Possible response: Primero leo el texto. Después escribo un resumen. Uso un diccionario porque hay palabras nuevas.
Other logical sequences are valid.

practice.prompt: Choose porque or por eso: “Estaba cansada; ___ me acosté temprano.” Explain.
hints: The second clause is a result.
Use the connector that introduces a consequence.
solution: Por eso is appropriate.
Tiredness is the reason and going to bed early is the result.
Estaba cansada; por eso me acosté temprano.
successCriteria: Tiredness is the reason and going to bed early is the result.
Estaba cansada; por eso me acosté temprano.

practice.prompt: Combine “El libro es largo” and “Me interesa” using aunque.
hints: The length is a possible obstacle.
solution: Aunque el libro es largo introduces a concession.
Me interesa states the continuing interest.
Aunque el libro es largo, me interesa.
successCriteria: Aunque el libro es largo introduces a concession.
Me interesa states the continuing interest.
Aunque el libro es largo, me interesa.

notes.title: Connectors in context
paragraphs: Connectors make logical relationships explicit, but they cannot repair ideas that do not fit together. Porque introduces a reason; por eso introduces a consequence. Aunque introduces a concession, and además adds another point. Distinguish chronology from causation: después says that one event follows another, not that the first caused it. Use a connector that matches the actual relationship and check the sentence on both sides. Variety is useful only when the meaning stays clear; repeating an accurate simple connector is better than misusing a more elaborate one.

workedExamples.prompt: Original task: link “No tenía mi cuaderno” and “Escribí en una hoja” as cause and consequence.
steps: The missing notebook supplies the reason.
Put the result after por eso: No tenía mi cuaderno; por eso escribí en una hoja.
workedExamples.conclusion: Alternatively, Escribí en una hoja porque no tenía mi cuaderno states the result before its reason.

flashcards.front: What follows porque?
flashcards.back: A reason.

flashcards.front: What follows por eso?
flashcards.back: A consequence or result.

flashcards.front: Does después prove causation?
flashcards.back: No; it marks a later event.

flashcards.front: What does además do?
flashcards.back: It adds a further point.

diagrams.title: Connectors: relationships to explain
diagrams.description: Cause → Consequence marker → Result. The connector introduces what followed because of that reason.

edges.label: The first statement supplies a reason.
The connector introduces what followed because of that reason.

lessons.summary: Practise a short exchange that answers, adds detail and invites a response while using appropriate forms of address.
explanation: Interaction requires listening to the other speaker and responding to their meaning, rather than reciting a prepared paragraph regardless of the question. A useful short turn answers, adds a reason or detail, and leaves space for a response. ¿Y tú? asks about an informal singular listener; ¿y usted? uses formal singular address. Tú and usted take different verb forms, so keep the chosen relationship consistent.

Repair phrases help communication when something is unclear. ¿Puedes repetirlo, por favor? asks an informal listener to repeat it; ¿Puede repetirlo, por favor? addresses someone as usted. Do not pretend to understand a word that changes the task. These written exchanges are rehearsal material; the page does not record pronunciation or measure spoken fluency. A partner can role-play them, with alternative relevant answers accepted when meaning, register and interaction are maintained.
keyIdeas: Answer before adding extra detail.
Maintain consistent forms of address.
Clarification is a communication strategy.

definitions.meaning: A contribution by one speaker in an exchange.
A follow-up question connected to what has just been said.
Language choices suited to the relationship, purpose and situation.

method: Identify what the other speaker asks.
Give a relevant answer and supporting detail.
Ask a follow-up or request clarification.
Check address forms and let the other speaker respond.

workedExample.prompt: Original role-play using informal tú: A asks “¿Qué haces los fines de semana?” Give an answer, reason and follow-up.
steps: Answer: Juego al baloncesto.
Reason: Me gusta porque puedo estar con mis amigos.
Follow-up: ¿Y tú, qué haces?
workedExample.conclusion: The response answers the weekend-activity question and invites the other speaker to contribute.

misconceptions.mistake: Reciting unrelated memorised material.
misconceptions.correction: Respond to the question and adapt the next turn.

misconceptions.mistake: Mixing tú and usted forms unintentionally.
misconceptions.correction: Keep the chosen form of address consistent.

practice.prompt: In a fictional informal exchange, answer “¿Te gusta leer?” with a positive answer beginning Sí and a reason.
solution: Possible response: Sí, me gusta leer porque aprendo cosas nuevas.
Other relevant reasons are valid.

practice.prompt: Ask a person addressed as usted: “Can you repeat it, please?”
hints: Use third-person singular puede for usted.
solution: ¿Puede repetirlo, por favor?
¿Podría repetirlo, por favor? is also a polite conditional alternative.

practice.prompt: Write a four-turn fictional tú dialogue that proposes meeting, asks the time, gives the time and accepts.
hints: Each turn should respond to the previous one.
solution: A: ¿Quieres ir al parque mañana?
B: Sí, ¿a qué hora?
A: A las cuatro.
B: De acuerdo. Nos vemos mañana. Other consistent times and plans are valid.

practice.prompt: A friend asks “¿Dónde estudias normalmente?” Give an answer, reason and follow-up in Spanish.
solution: Normalmente estudio en la biblioteca.
Me gusta porque hay poco ruido.
¿Y tú, dónde estudias?
successCriteria: Me gusta porque hay poco ruido.

practice.prompt: You do not understand “horario”. Ask politely what it means rather than guessing.
solution: Perdona, no entiendo la palabra “horario”.
¿Qué significa?
This identifies the precise difficulty and invites clarification instead of pretending to understand.
successCriteria: This identifies the precise difficulty and invites clarification instead of pretending to understand.

notes.title: Speaking interaction in context
paragraphs: Interaction requires listening and responding to another speaker, not only delivering a memorised paragraph. Give an answer, add a relevant detail and invite the other person to continue. Clarification phrases help maintain communication when a word or instruction is unclear. Match tú and usted consistently to the relationship specified in the task. A follow-up question should connect to what was said rather than changing the subject abruptly. In rehearsal, record which part of the exchange broke down and practise that function with new content.

workedExamples.prompt: Original role-play: a friend says “Me gusta dibujar paisajes”. Respond with a connection and a follow-up question.
steps: Acknowledge the idea: A mí también me gusta dibujar.
Ask for a relevant detail: ¿Prefieres dibujar montañas o ciudades?
workedExamples.conclusion: The response continues the topic and gives the partner a clear opportunity to answer.

flashcards.front: How do you ask a friend to repeat?
flashcards.back: ¿Puedes repetirlo, por favor?

flashcards.front: How can you request a slower pace?
flashcards.back: ¿Puedes hablar más despacio, por favor?

flashcards.front: What makes a follow-up relevant?
flashcards.back: It responds to information the partner has just supplied.

flashcards.front: Why avoid only memorised monologues?
flashcards.back: They may not address the partner’s actual contribution or question.

diagrams.title: Speaking interaction: relationships to explain
diagrams.description: Listen → Respond → Extend. A linked question keeps the exchange open.

edges.label: The response uses the partner’s information.
A linked question keeps the exchange open.

lessons.summary: Read an original short Spanish text for gist, precise detail and supported inference without adding unstated information.
explanation: Start by identifying the type of text and its likely purpose, then read for the overall message. A notice may give practical information; an email may explain a plan or change. On a second reading, locate the words answering the question. Watch for no, nunca and contrast markers, because they can reverse an interpretation. A familiar word alone is not enough to answer the whole question.

Use context to propose a meaning for an unfamiliar word, then check whether it fits the sentence. Do not add a reason, place or feeling that the text does not supply. A supported inference is narrower than an invented story. These passages are original fictional texts, so answers should refer to their wording rather than outside facts. If a task asks for English, preserve the Spanish meaning; if it asks for Spanish, a concise accurate paraphrase may be better than copying unrelated lines.
keyIdeas: Read for gist before detail.
Negation and contrast matter.
An inference needs textual support.

definitions.meaning: The main message of a text.
Information directly stated in the text.
An interpretation supported by clues but not directly stated in the same words.

method: Identify text type and purpose.
Read once for the main message.
Locate evidence for the exact question.
Check negation and avoid unsupported additions.

workedExample.prompt: Original fictional notice: “La biblioteca abre a las nueve. Los viernes cierra a las seis, no a las cinco.” State Friday’s closing time in English.
steps: The question asks when it closes, not opens.
Los viernes identifies Friday; cierra a las seis gives the time.
No a las cinco rejects five o’clock.
workedExample.conclusion: It closes at six o’clock on Fridays. The notice does not specify opening or closing times for every other day.

misconceptions.mistake: Answering with the first number seen.
misconceptions.correction: Match the number to the action asked about.

misconceptions.mistake: Adding a reason not stated in the passage.
misconceptions.correction: Separate the text’s information from speculation.

practice.prompt: Read the original fictional message: “No puedo ir hoy. Nos vemos mañana.” When does the writer propose meeting? Answer in English.
hints: The second sentence gives the new plan.
solution: Tomorrow.
The message says the writer cannot go today; it does not explain why.

practice.prompt: Original fictional text: “A Lucía le gusta el parque, pero hoy prefiere quedarse en casa porque llueve.” Explain in English why she prefers staying home today.
solution: She prefers to stay home because it is raining.
This does not mean she dislikes the park; the first clause says she likes it.

practice.prompt: Original fictional email: “Gracias por invitarme. Llegaré después de la clase.” Identify the stated plan and one detail the email does not establish. Answer in English.
solution: The writer plans to arrive after the class.
The exact arrival time is not given.
The text also does not establish how long the class lasts.

practice.prompt: Original notice: “El museo cierra los lunes, pero la tienda abre todos los días.” Is the shop open on Mondays? Explain.
hints: Identify the subject of each clause.
solution: Yes, the shop is open on Mondays according to the notice.
The Monday closure applies to the museum.
Pero distinguishes the shop’s daily opening from the museum’s schedule.
successCriteria: Yes, the shop is open on Mondays according to the notice.
The Monday closure applies to the museum.
Pero distinguishes the shop’s daily opening from the museum’s schedule.

practice.prompt: Original sentence: “Ana prestó su diccionario a Luis porque él no tenía uno.” Who lacked a dictionary, and what supports this?
hints: Track the recipient of the loan.
solution: Luis lacked a dictionary.
Él refers to Luis in this sentence.
That lack explains why Ana lent her dictionary to him.
successCriteria: Él refers to Luis in this sentence.
That lack explains why Ana lent her dictionary to him.

notes.title: Reading comprehension in context
paragraphs: Reading comprehension requires evidence for the answer, not a plausible guess based on the topic. Read the question first to identify whether it asks for time, reason, person or opinion. Then locate the relevant sentence and inspect negation, corrections and contrast words. Pronouns may refer back to a noun in an earlier sentence. Familiar-looking words can mislead, so test them in context. When answering in English, preserve the meaning rather than translating word by word. Do not add background knowledge that the text does not establish.

workedExamples.prompt: Original fictional notice: “El taller empieza a las cuatro. La recepción abre media hora antes. No hace falta traer materiales.” When does reception open, and what must participants bring?
steps: The workshop starts at 4:00; half an hour earlier is 3:30.
No hace falta negates necessity, so materials are not required.
workedExamples.conclusion: Reception opens at 3:30, and participants do not need to bring materials.

flashcards.front: What does no hace falta mean?
flashcards.back: It is not necessary.

flashcards.front: Why check contrast words?
flashcards.back: They may revise or limit an earlier statement.

flashcards.front: What should support a comprehension answer?
flashcards.back: A relevant detail or inference grounded in the supplied text.

flashcards.front: How should an unfamiliar word be approached?
flashcards.back: Use context and grammatical clues, then verify rather than relying on resemblance alone.

nodes.detail: Find reception time and required items.

nodes.label: Textual evidence
nodes.detail: Media hora antes; no hace falta.

lessons.summary: Plan gist and detail listening, track corrections and distinguish transcript rehearsal from an actual audio assessment.
objectives: Use a repeat listening for a specific uncertainty.
explanation: Before listening, identify the information you need: a destination, reason, time or attitude. On a first hearing, focus on the main message rather than trying to write every word. A later hearing can test a specific detail. Note changes such as no..., sino... or a speaker correcting a time. The final confirmed information may differ from the first number mentioned.

This page contains original scripts and transcript-based strategy exercises, not playable recordings. For a listening rehearsal, a partner or teacher can read a script naturally while the learner looks away, then repeat it for a stated detail. Reading the visible script alone is not evidence of listening ability. In an actual assessment, follow its rules about repetitions and notes. The model answers here show how to interpret the supplied words; they do not assess pronunciation recognition, accent familiarity or listening fluency.
keyIdeas: Choose a focus before listening.
Track corrections rather than isolated words.
A visible transcript is not an audio test.

definitions.meaning: Understanding the overall message.
Listening for a particular required detail.
A correction that replaces earlier information.

method: Read the question and predict the type of information needed.
Listen for the main message.
Use an allowed repeat to resolve a specific detail.
Check corrections and distinguish certainty from guesses.

workedExample.prompt: Original script for partner read-aloud: “El autobús sale a las tres... perdón, a las tres y media.” What departure time is finally given? The visible script is rehearsal support, not an audio test.
steps: The first time is three o’clock.
Perdón signals a correction.
The corrected time is las tres y media, half past three.
workedExample.conclusion: The final departure time is 3:30. A learner using only the printed script has practised interpretation, not demonstrated listening proficiency.

misconceptions.mistake: Keeping the first number despite a correction.
misconceptions.correction: Listen through the correction and record the confirmed detail.

misconceptions.mistake: Calling a correct transcript answer proof of listening fluency.
misconceptions.correction: Use an actual listening task to assess auditory comprehension.

practice.prompt: Transcript-based strategy exercise, not an audio test: “El club no se reúne el martes, sino el jueves.” Which day is confirmed? Answer in English.
solution: Thursday is confirmed; Tuesday is rejected.

practice.prompt: For a partner-read fictional announcement, you understand the destination but are unsure of the departure time. State a specific goal for an allowed second listening.
solution: Listen for the departure-time expression and any correction following it.
Keep the already understood destination as a working note, but verify it if the repeat contradicts it.

practice.prompt: Plan a two-pass listening rehearsal using an original short travel script and a partner. Explain how to avoid turning it into a reading task.
hints: Separate the learner from the visible script.
solution: The partner reads while the learner looks away; the first pass targets the overall journey or message.
The second pass targets the required time or place and any correction.
Compare with the transcript afterwards; follow actual assessment rules when practising for a specific test.

practice.prompt: Original read-aloud script: “Traed dos lápices; no, mejor tres.” What quantity is finally requested?
solution: The first quantity is two.
No, mejor introduces a revision.
The final requested quantity is three pencils.
successCriteria: The final requested quantity is three pencils.

practice.prompt: Original script: “El tren llega a las diez, pero sale a las diez y veinte.” Give arrival and departure separately.
hints: Do not treat the later time as a correction.
solution: Arrival is at 10:00.
Departure is at 10:20.
Pero contrasts two different events; the second time does not replace the arrival time.
successCriteria: Pero contrasts two different events; the second time does not replace the arrival time.

checklist: I distinguish reading from listening evidence.

notes.title: Listening strategies in context
paragraphs: Listening often requires holding an early possibility in mind until a speaker corrects or completes it. Listen for repair markers such as perdón, mejor dicho and no... sino. Write brief notes rather than trying to transcribe every word. For numbers and times, separate the final confirmed information from discarded alternatives. A visible script is useful for rehearsal and checking, but it does not measure independent listening. Practise with a partner reading the original script aloud, then compare the answer with the precise words that support it.

workedExamples.prompt: Original script for partner read-aloud: “La reunión es en la sala quince... perdón, en la cincuenta. Empieza a las dos.” Identify the final room and time.
steps: The repair marker perdón cancels the first room number, quince.
The corrected room is cincuenta, and the separate time is las dos.
workedExamples.conclusion: The final information is Room 50 at 2:00. This written script is rehearsal material, not an audio recording.

flashcards.front: What can perdón signal during speech?
flashcards.back: A correction of information just given.

flashcards.front: What should notes retain after a correction?
flashcards.back: The final confirmed detail, with earlier alternatives crossed out if necessary.

flashcards.front: Why avoid full transcription during a short task?
flashcards.back: It can distract from the requested information and later corrections.

flashcards.front: Does reading a script establish listening skill?
flashcards.back: No; independent listening requires hearing the material without reading it.
